title: Folding literals fixes each initially free variable
statement: Fix $n$ variables, let $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean assignment, let $\rho$ be a restriction on these variables, and let $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_m$ be a list of literals. Process the literals from left to right, maintaining a current restriction that begins as $\rho$: at each literal $\ell$, if its underlying variable $\ell.\mathrm{var}$ is free in the current restriction, update that restriction by fixing $\ell.\mathrm{var}$ to the value $x(\ell.\mathrm{var})$, and otherwise leave the restriction unchanged; write $\rho^*$ for the restriction obtained after the whole list has been processed. Then for every literal $\ell$ in the list whose variable is free in the original restriction $\rho$, the value $\rho^*(\ell.\mathrm{var})$ is set, i.e.\ $\ell.\mathrm{var}$ is not free in $\rho^*$.
hypotheses_covered: l is a member of the list lits
l.var is free in the initial restriction ρ
ρ* is the left fold over lits with the update-if-free step starting from ρ
replaced:
